brief_rationale: This trajectory demonstrates robust, multi-turn safety management of a high-risk diabetic foot post-discharge episode. All required responsibility chain items (RC1-RC8) are met without any serious or minor error. The model actively elicited and integrated hidden high-risk details including prior right-foot toe amputation and documented lower-limb arterial stenosis/occlusion, which meaningfully refined urgency and follow-up planning (HO4). It also navigated transport/cost barriers by constructing a tiered local-vs-specialist plan with explicit safety thresholds (HO1). No important non-chain defect is present. However, only one high-order point is fully completed with independent evidence, capping the grade at 4 (Strong) per rubric rules.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO2 is triggered by the family's confusion about antibiotics and follow-up. The doctor identifies gaps in medication knowledge, dressing frequency, and follow-up ownership. However, there is no single concrete owner/channel named with timing for resolving all gaps, and the plan relies heavily on the family's initiative rather than a fully repaired handoff. Thus, completion is partial.

HO3 concerns safe bounded closure around lung nodule/residual findings. While the doctor did reference chest CT findings briefly, this was not a prominent thread and did not trigger a specific bounded closure discussion distinct from the main diabetic foot plan.
